params.body:
Everything else this machine needs sits in a manifest: npm packages in
`package.json`, models in `store/model-config.json`, secrets in
`declaredCredentials()`. The command-line programs were the exception, and they
are the ones no installer puts back. They arrived by hand on a box nobody has
rebuilt yet, and a dependency written down nowhere does not exist: a rebuilt box
learns about it at the moment the work fails.

Not hypothetical. Gentells' public site did this with poppler: the command to
publish a report stopped on `pdftoppm ontbreekt` on a machine with no sudo to
fix it. Here the same poppler tools have been assumed present for months, and
`claude` has twice gone quiet without a word.

## What this adds

`GET /api/elixir` now carries `extra.binaries`: what this app calls, whether it
can see it, **who calls it** and **what stops working without it**.

```json
{"name": "pdftoppm", "required": true, "found": true, "path": "/usr/bin/pdftoppm",
 "where": "packages/core/report-render.mjs",
 "why": "rasterising the open pages of a report; without it no report can be published"}
```

It does not judge. How bad an absence is depends on what leans on it, and that
belongs with Elixir like every other threshold (abovebeyond-ai/elixir#223).

## The list is kept honest by a test

`test/binaries.test.mjs` reads the source and fails when a program is called
that is not declared. A hand-kept declaration that falls behind is worse than
none: it is a measurement that says everything is present while something is
missing.

Writing it turned up one nobody would have named from memory: **curl**, which
`ingest-drive.mjs` shells out to. The reverse check also holds, so the list
cannot grow entries nothing calls.

Fourteen programs declared, nine required. All fourteen are present on the
Observatory box today, so this raises nothing now; it makes the dependency
visible before the next rebuild does.

716 tests pass, 4 new.
params.title: Declare the programs this app shells out to
